record.paper_title: Major Unsolved Problems in Space Plasma Physics
record.original_question: How do the three-dimensional structures of interplanetary turbulent magnetic fields determine energetic-particle transport in the heliosphere, including pitch-angle scattering parallel to the background magnetic field, transverse diffusion across magnetic-field lines, stochastic field-line diffusion, whether solar energetic particles from flares and coronal mass ejections reach Earth, and the 22-year modulation of galactic cosmic rays by solar magnetic fields?

evidence.quote: the three-dimensional properties that determine how both solar energetic particles and galactic cosmic rays propagate throughout the heliosphere
Planar, parallel-propagating Alfv?n waves are efficient pitch-angle scatterers (Jokipii, 1971), but only inefficiently transport particles across field lines.
quasi-two-dimensional turbulence causes field lines to diffuse stochastically, which should lead to significant perpendicular diffusion.

artifact.category_tag: energetic-particle transport in turbulent magnetic fields
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of deriving energetic-particle transport coefficients (parallel and perpendicular diffusion, field-line random walk) from the 3D structure of interplanetary turbulence, and explaining solar-energetic-particle propagation and 22-year cosmic-ray modulation, remains an active open research area. Quasi-linear theory (Jokipii 1966/1971), nonlinear guiding center theory (Matthaeus et al. 2003), and unified nonlinear theories (Shalchi) provide partial results, but a complete first-principles theory is not yet established.

status_evidence.title: Nonlinear theory of perpendicular transport (Matthaeus et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Nonlinear guiding center theory relates perpendicular diffusion to field-line diffusion and parallel scattering, but is approximate.
status_evidence.claim: Theory of perpendicular transport is incomplete and approximate.

status_evidence.title: A. Shalchi, Nonlinear Cosmic Ray Diffusion Theories (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: A monograph surveying still-open problems in deriving cosmic-ray diffusion coefficients from turbulence properties.
status_evidence.claim: Comprehensive derivation of transport coefficients from 3D turbulence remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Potgieter, Solar Modulation of Cosmic Rays, Living Rev. Solar Phys.
status_evidence.snippet: 22-year modulation involving drifts and polarity reversal is modeled but not fully predicted from first principles.
status_evidence.claim: 22-year cosmic-ray modulation lacks a complete first-principles theory.
